# Carapaz

**Status: DRAFT** · world: [superearth](../lore/worlds/superearth.md) · kind: new · stage: space · id: `carapaz`

## Niche

- **Habitat:** Volcanic scree slopes, fog belts, shallow shelf edges
- **Diet:** Opportunistic omnivore; crushes calcified fungi, catches falling fruit, scavenges carrion
- **Active:** Crepuscular
- **Predators:** none

## Body

Bivalve-convergent lineage. Fused, flattened carapace of chitin-mineral composite. Four lateral walking legs with stiff joints. Massive asymmetrical claws. Visceral mass retracts fully under shield. Copper-veined hemolymph visible through translucent carapace edge.

**Temperament:** Cautious, territorial, anchors deeply; slow to engage but relentless once committed

### carapaz.c1: Flattened, reinforced carapace

Trait ← Flattened profile minimizes drag in dense air and lowers center of mass under high gravity ← High density increases drag force; high gravity increases toppling torque ← F8: 10 bar atmosphere, ~12.5 kg/m³ density ← F4: 1.85g surface gravity ← F8, F4

- **Skill:** Anchor Plate (Defence): Locks claws into substrate, reducing incoming damage by 30% and preventing displacement.
- **Weakness:** Slow to right itself if overturned.
- **Observe:**
  1. Carapaz flattens against rock during gusts.
  2. Scree shifts under its weight without it tipping.
  3. Claws bite deep into stone.
- **Journal:** The pressure and gravity demanded a low profile; everything else followed.
- **Plausibility:** plausible (judge astrobio/autoloop-2026-11-19, 2026-11-19)
  - On 1.85 g (F4), a low, wide body lowers the center of mass and cuts overturning torque on scree; in ~10 bar, dense air (F8) raises form drag on tall profiles, favouring a flattened shield. Chitin–mineral composites are a standard way to buy stiffness per unit mass at high structural loads—same scaling logic as exoskeletal armouring on Earth.

## Journal

- EN: They walk sideways because the wind and the scree leave no other way.
- EN: A wink at carcinisation? No; just the physics of 1.85g and 10 bar squeezing everything flat and lateral.

## Secrets

- Their copper-rich blood neutralizes sulfide toxins from volcanic vents.
- They can detect pressure changes in the air to predict fog fronts hours in advance.

## Moments

- When the amber fog rolls in, the scree goes silent as a dozen Carapaz lock their claws into the stone and vanish into their shells, leaving only the rhythmic hiss of ventilation and the faint blue glow of their copper blood.
